title: Christ's healing grace is efficacious of itself
source_text: V. Itaque, ex eorum mente, omnis vera & proprie ac speciali modo sic dicta Christi gratia, aegro homini sanando comparata, & ad singulos piae voluntatis affectus & motus necessaria, gratia per se efficax est, & talis ut a nullo duro corde unquam respuatur: quippe quae semper velle donat, & cordis duritiem aufert, pro mensura doni divini. Ac quanquam homo si vult, illi dissentire potest, semper tamen efficit ut homo illi non dissentiat, nec dissentire velit.
pass_a_gloss: V. Therefore, in their mind, every true and properly and in a special way so called grace of Christ, fitted for healing sick man, and necessary for each affection and motion of pious will, is grace efficacious by itself, and such that by no hard heart is it ever rejected: as that which always gives willing, and takes away the hardness of the heart, according to the measure of the divine gift. And although man if he wills, can dissent from it, yet it always brings it about that man does not dissent from it, nor wish to dissent.
pass_b_english: Thesis V. On their view, then, all true grace of Christ, properly and specifically so called, the grace suited to heal sick humanity and needed for every devout affection and movement of the will, is efficacious of itself. No hard heart ever rejects it, because it always grants the willing and removes hardness of heart in proportion to the divine gift.
A person can withhold consent from it if he chooses; yet it always ensures that he does not withhold consent, and does not want to.

lemmas.latin: a nullo duro corde unquam respuatur
lemmas.gloss: by no hard heart is it ever rejected
according to the measure of the divine gift

choices.why: Jansenist and Thomist formula: grace whose efficacy comes from the grace itself, not from the consent that follows.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris.
